analysis:
Only base-side text of .github/workflows/release-swift.yml was supplied (lines 1-1243). No patch hunks or head text were included, so the PR's actual change is not visible and cannot be evaluated; this is a coverage limit, not evidence the change is safe. Security-relevant base behavior for the integration pass to compare against the head:
- resolve-env (lines 148-192) checks out master and runs `provider-release-resume.py verify-source` before any credentials are used.
- build-provider (194-247) and qualify-sdk (249-268) run without secrets. Builds are stamped with DARKBLOOM_RELEASE_ENVIRONMENT, and the unsigned artifact is bound to the source SHA and version.
- build-and-release (270-971) imports the Developer ID certificate and provisioning profile. It requires aps-environment=production and an access group, and rejects get-task-allow=true. It signs the fan helper with its own identifier and no provider entitlements. It runs the pre-sign and final-bundle runtime-smoke checks, notarizes and staples, then computes the binary, CDHash and bundle hashes. The CDHash feeds A-017/T-054 qualification, so any change to its derivation or to the entitlement checks matters.
- Prod R2/coordinator/release secrets are gated on the resolved environment being prod (lines 306-315, 1011-1029, 1113-1137). A dev run must never receive them (A-005, A-011).
- stage-release (978-1077) and publish-release (1079-1187) download a retained publication artifact by ID and digest, then register with the coordinator through the release key and update aliases.
- Unpinned `pip install awscli` appears at lines 1067 and 1175, in jobs that hold R2 and release keys. This is pre-existing.
- validate-older-macos (1189-1243) is a smoke test on an older OS.
The next pass should diff the head against these controls: secret gating, artifact digest binding, entitlement and hash checks, and the permissions blocks.
